question: Ethanol is formed during:
solution:
The correct answer is __**anaerobic respiration in yeasts**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanol is produced during anaerobic respiration in yeasts**
 
• Anaerobic** respiration is a process that occurs when oxygen is not availabl**e, and it produces ethanol and carbon dioxide as byproducts.
 
• This process is also known as alcoholic fermentation.
 
• In yeast, glucose is used to produce ethanol and carbon dioxide.
 
• In contrast, aerobic respiration occurs in muscle fibres during everyday activities and light exercise.
 
• Aerobic respiration requires oxygen to break down food energy and generate ATP for muscle contractions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Aerobic respiration in muscles:**

 
 
• Like yeasts, muscles can also undergo aerobic respiration in the presence of oxygen.
 
• This process breaks down glucose to produce carbon dioxide and water.
 
• It is the primary source of energy for muscles during moderate activity.
 
 
 
• **Anaerobic respiration in muscles**:
 
 
• This process occurs in muscles when oxygen supply is limited, such as during intense exercise.
 
• In the absence of oxygen, muscles break down glucose to produce lactic acid.
 
• Lactic acid buildup can cause muscle fatigue and soreness
